{{recipesummary|category=Pork recipes|servings=6–8 persons|difficulty=3}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|United States]]

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Quart|quarts]] shelled [[Cookbook:Lima Bean|lima beans]]
*24 ears of [[Cookbook:Maize|corn]] cut off the cob
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] pickled [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] (optional)
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking sugar|sugar]] (optional)
*2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==

# If using pork, cover pork with water, and [[Cookbook:Parboiling|parboil]] it.
# Add beans, then corn, sugar, butter, and pepper to taste. After corn is added, watch carefully to keep from scorching.
# Serve.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* A chopped red bell pepper can be added.
* Note that lima beans that have not been cooked should be thoroughly boiled for at least 10 minutes to rid the beans of phytohemagglutinin, a toxin found in uncooked lima beans. Canned beans are safe to eat without cooking. 

==References==
* Mrs. S. A. Powers, “New England Succotash” in {{Gutenberg|1084|name=Recipes Tried and True}}
